records.name: Pennypack Ecological Restoration Trust
records.summary: A land trust that cares for a nature preserve along Pennypack Creek in Huntingdon Valley, just over the city line from Northeast Philadelphia. Volunteers pull invasive vines off trees and help staff with restoration projects.
records.what_you_do: Free-A-Tree workdays cut invasive vines off trees on the first Saturday of the month, October through April. Service Day mornings work on an active restoration project with staff. Bring gloves and pruning shears, or borrow theirs.

schedule.text: Free-A-Tree workdays on the first Saturday of each month, October through April. A Service Day runs around Presidents Day (the 2026 one was Monday, Feb 16, 10 am to 12 pm).

locations.label: Trust headquarters
locations.address: 2955 Edge Hill Road, Huntingdon Valley, PA 19006

cost.text: Not stated on the pages read

first_step.how: Register through the Trust's volunteer sign-up link before the date (Free-A-Tree and Service Day both ask for pre-registration), or call the office at 215.657.0830
first_step.basis: The Trust says volunteers learn restoration from staff, says groups and individuals are welcome, and publishes a sign-up link.

records.notes: Trust office is in Huntingdon Valley (Montgomery County). Its trails and work sites are in Pennypack Park, which runs into Philadelphia, but some work may be outside city limits, so check before going. The Service Day page gives its start as 10 pm in one spot and 10 am in another; 10 am is used here and should be confirmed. Streamkeepers and ReForesters programs are named on the site but were not read. Cost not stated on the pages read. Friends of Pennypack Park is listed in leads_only. Corrected by the orchestrator 2026-10-08: the preserve is in Huntingdon Valley; the earlier Pennypack Park, Philadelphia location was an assumption.

notes: one corrected record after the spot check
